rules.title: Annual rent increase cap: lesser of 3% or 80% of CPI change
rules.requirement: A landlord may raise rent by no more than the lesser of 3% of current rent or 80% of the CPI change per year, per the city's summary of the Rent Stabilization and Just Cause Eviction Ordinance.
rules.citation: https://santa-ana.gov/departments/rent-stabilization (City of Santa Ana Rent Stabilization page; ordinance number/section not stated in source)
rules.quoted_span: The increase cannot be more than 3% of your current rent or 80% of the Consumer Price Index (CPI) change, whichever is less.
rules.key_value: lesser of 3% or 80% of CPI change
rules.interaction: The currently published annual maximum (2.87% for 2026-09-01 through 2027-08-31) is the output of this formula as presented on the page.

rules.quoted_span: 2.87 percent is the maximum allowable rent increase for the period of September 1, 2026 through August 31, 2027.
rules.interaction: Annual figure under the general cap (lesser of 3% or 80% of CPI change). Applies for the stated period only.

rules.title: Landlord must have a valid reason to evict
rules.requirement: A landlord must have a valid (just) cause to evict a tenant, such as nonpayment of rent, breach of lease, or the landlord moving into the property, per the city's summary. The page's list of reasons is illustrative; the full list of authorized causes is not provided in this chunk.
